items.rationale: Both conclusions first said the T allele was "about 6 in 100 copies in Finland", which I had taken from Hirvonen 2017's citation of 1000 Genomes (0.056). frequencies.csv, written by enrich_facts from gnomAD v4.1 joint, gives 2.4% in the Finnish population over 17394 individuals against 1000 Genomes' ~99 Finnish samples, and 2.2% globally. I corrected the lay wording to about 4 in 100 people carrying one copy and about 95 in 100 carrying none, computed from the gnomAD global counts. The paper's figure is not wrong for its source, it is a far smaller sample, and the module should quote the better-powered one. No association claim, direction, state or weight changed. Checked both sides before editing: the disagreement is sample size, not a stale archive. Source said: T allele 847/34788 = 2.4% in Finnish; 12545/574784 = 2.2% global; 183 homozygotes in 287392 individuals. [jmc field=conclusion value_sha256=ebecddf3fbb2 source=gnomad_v4.1_joint recorded=2026-11-25T23:25:42Z by=claude-opus-5]

items.rationale: validate_module reported a genotype coverage gap: the module stated C/C and C/T at this site and not T/T. gnomAD settles that T/T people exist in numbers a consumer will meet - 183 homozygotes, about 1 in 1570 - so leaving the genotype unrowed means a real carrier runs this module and matches nothing. Neither study observed a T/T individual (Hirvonen reports only heterozygotes; Sheikholmolouki reports 8 heterozygotes and no homozygote), so there is no evidence to state a direction from. I wrote state=alt deliberately: it is the genotype descriptor that carries no direction and derives to direction=unknown, where neutral would assert the genotype is benign and risk would assert a sign no study measured. weight is left blank rather than 0.0 because 0.0 is a claim that this genotype changes nothing, which is exactly what is unknown. The conclusion says plainly that nothing has measured two copies and that the one-copy finding may not be read as a double dose. The alternative was to drop the genotype, which would have been silent rather than honest. Source said: 183 T/T homozygotes in 287392 individuals = about 1 in 1570; neither PMID 28399814 nor PMID 41249831 observed a single T/T individual. items.rationale: studies.csv has no column stating which way an odds ratio runs, and this row pairs effect_size=3.58 with effect_allele=T and n_cases=106 (the longer-living men), which can be read as T raising the odds of long survival - the exact opposite of the finding. I recomputed the OR from the paper's own counts: longer-living 3 T of 212 alleles (HBCS 1/43 het plus HBS 2/63 het), earlier-death controls 9 T of 184 alleles, giving (9/175)/(3/209) = 3.583. That reproduces 3.58 to three figures, which establishes two things: the estimate is allelic rather than carrier-level (the carrier calculation gives 3.72), and it is oriented towards the earlier-death group. The paper disagrees with itself here - abstract 3.53, Results text and Table 2 both 3.58 - and the recomputation settles it on 3.58. I stated the orientation in prose in the three free-text cells rather than changing any number, because no number was wrong; what was missing was the direction the number runs in. Source said: OR 3.58, 95% CI 0.96-13.4, p = 0.074 (Hirvonen 2017 Table 2); abstract states 3.53.
